summary: multyproccess ships an install-time infostealer dropper impersonating the Python Software Foundation
details: The package impersonates the Python Software Foundation and mimics 'multiprocessing'/'requests' via forged setup.py metadata (author='Python Software Foundation', author_email='python-dev@python.org', url='github.com/psf/request'). A custom install/develop cmdclass in setup.py base64-decodes request/.payload, writes it to a temp.py file, and spawns it as a detached background process (pythonw.exe with DETACHED_PROCESS on Windows, start_new_session on Unix), so the payload runs automatically on `pip install`. The decoded 659KB Python payload self-identifies as a 'PROFESSIONAL INFOSTEALER' targeting Chrome/Edge/Brave/Firefox Login Data, cookies, autofill and credit-card stores, Firefox key4.db, 50+ crypto-wallet browser extensions and standalone wallets (Electrum, Binance, Ethereum keystores), 2FA extensions, and email/FTP client credentials. Collected data is exfiltrated to api.telegram.org bot endpoints (sendMessage/sendDocument) and to recloud-blush.vercel.app, with ipinfo.io used for geolocation. The payload additionally advertises persistence disguised as svchost.exe, keylogging targeting passwords/seeds/private keys, and periodic screenshots with real-time Telegram/C2 notifications.
